["59804", "CHEK8TIMI JUSQU’OÙ L’EAU EST PROFONDE…UNE HISTOIRE QUI SE FAÇONNE", "Vivez une expérience immersive au cœur de l’histoire du poste de traite de Chicoutimi grâce à cette exposition interactive historique et archéologique. L’histoire de la région étant intimement liée à sa géographie, l’objectif principal de l’exposition est de raconter cette histoire par la lunette du site historique du POSTE DE TRAITE DE CHICOUTIMI, à la fois à l’intérieur du musée dans une salle d’exposition et à l’extérieur directement sur le site de l’ancien poste de traite de Chicoutimi.

Grâce à 2 mini tablettes, il est maintenant possible de visionner le reportage de La Fabrique Culturelle sur le POSTE DE TRAITE DE CHICOUTIMI réalisé en août 2018 avec l’archéologue de l’UQAC Érik Langevin. Cet ajout permettra aux visiteurs de faire plus facilement le lien entre l’exposition CHEK8TIMI et le POSTE DE TRAITE DE CHICOUTIMI et de mieux comprendre l’importance de ce site patrimonial d’importance.
Berceau de l’occupation du territoire, Le Poste de traite de Chicoutimi

Il côtoie les artistes améri-cains qui sont parmi les premiers étrangers à découvrir la Bretagne, fondant à Pont-Aven et à Concarneau de véritables colonies artistiques. La fileuse, peinte par le jeune Paul Peel dans son atelier parisien, sera une des premières œuvres canadiennes à entrer dans la collection de l'Art Association of Montreal. Formé à la peinture académique, Peel en applique les principes : il organise la composition autour d'un personnage central et traite les modelés avec précision. Décor et accessoires appuient ici une volonté manifeste de pittoresque. La fileuse, probablement un modèle professionnel, est vêtue d'un costume breton et porte la petite coiffe typique de la région de Rosporden, dans le sud du Finistère. Elle tient à la main une quenouille ; derrière elle, un enfant dort dans un lit clos. ["A", "Catégorie", "Habiletés", "Aptitudes innées et développées facilitant l’acquisition de connaissances et de compétences requises pour effectuer le travail attendu."]
["A.01", "Sous-catégorie", "Habiletés cognitives", "Habiletés ayant une incidence sur l’acquisition et l’application de connaissances dans l’exécution de diverses activités mentales au travail."]
["A.01.a", "Groupe de similitude", "Habiletés à générer des idées et à raisonner", ""]

["A.01.a.01", "Descripteur", "Ordonner de l’information", "L’habileté à disposer des éléments ou des actions dans un certain ordre ou un modèle, conformément à une règle spécifique ou à un ensemble de règles comme les séquences de chiffres, de lettres, de mots, d’images et d’opérations mathématiques."]
["A.01.a.02", "Descripteur", "Souplesse dans la catégorisation", "L’habileté à générer ou à utiliser un ensemble de règles pour combiner ou regrouper des choses de différentes façons."]
["A.01.a.03", "Descripteur", "Raisonnement déductif", "L’habileté à appliquer des règles générales pour formuler des réponses logiques à des problèmes spécifiques."]

["A.01.a.04", "Descripteur", "Raisonnement inductif", "L’habileté à combiner des éléments d’information pour former des règles générales ou des conclusions, ce qui comprend de trouver une relation entre des événements apparemment sans liens."]
["A.01.a.05", "Descripteur", "Facilité à concevoir des idées", "L’habileté à imaginer plusieurs idées sur un même sujet."]

["A.01.a.06", "Descripteur", "Détection de problèmes", "L’habileté à identifier un problème existant ou potentiel. Il ne s'agit pas de résoudre le problème, mais seulement d’en reconnaître la présence."]
["A.01.b.01", "Descripteur", "Habileté numériques", "L’habileté à effectuer des opérations arithmétiques telles que des additions, des soustractions, des multiplications et des divisions."]
["A.01.b.02", "Descripteur", "Raisonnement mathématique", "L’habileté à choisir les bonnes méthodes ou formules mathématiques pour résoudre un problème."]
["A.01.c.01", "Descripteur", "Mémorisation", "L’habileté à se souvenir d’informations tels que des mots, des chiffres, des images ou des procédures."]

["A.01.c.02", "Descripteur", "Tâches multiples", "L’habileté à alterner entre deux ou plusieurs activités ou sources d’information comme des conversations, des sons, le toucher ou d’autres stimuli, pendant la même période."]

["A.01.c.03", "Descripteur", "Identification de motifs", "L'habileté à identifier, à repérer ou à détecter un motif connu, tel qu'une figure, un objet, un mot ou un son, qui est dissimulé parmi d'autres informations ou matériaux."]
["A.01.c.04", "Descripteur", "Vitesse d’organisation de motifs", "L’habileté à combiner et à organiser rapidement de l’information pour obtenir des structures ou modèles significatifs."]

["A.01.c.05", "Descripteur", "Vitesse de perception", "L’habileté à comparer avec rapidité et précision les similitudes et les différences entre des ensembles de lettres, de chiffres, d’objets, d’images ou de modèles. Les éléments à comparer peuvent être présentés en même temps, l'un après l'autre ou à partir d'un objet mémorisé."]

["2018", "Q2018-01", "Ministry of Community Safety and Correctional Services (MCSCS)", "1. Implementation of EMR (Electronic Medical Records) by the Ministry of Community Safety and Correctional Services and their facilities.", "The Ministry of Community Safety and Correctional Services (MCSCS) is working with the Ministry of Health and Long-Term Care (MOHLTC) to review requirements for the acquisition of an enterprise-wide electronic health record (EHR) solution for all correctional facilities to:
a. Improve ability to document and monitor client health status over time; 
b. Facilitate continuity of care through improved communications; Inform clinical decisions, such as how to best utilize staff and services towards improving health care outcomes; and
c. Provide data to inform planning and training needs for continuous improvement.

The current focus of MCSCS is to build upon the work that has been done previously to evaluate options for automation solutions that do not preclude any future changes to the current service delivery model. An enterprise-wide, fully integrated EHR remains a strategic priority for the ministry.", "", "", "", "", "", ""]

["2018", "Q2018-01", "MCSCS", "2. Quinte Detention Centre to follow the Ministry of Community Safety and Correction Services standards and guidelines with specific attention to Methadone Maintenance Treatment policy.", "The MCSCS Methadone Maintenance Treatment (MMT) Policy and Procedure align with the College of Physician and Surgeons on Ontario Guidelines for MMT. The MCSCS recently revised its policy and procedure to clarify and broaden initiation of treatment to address the elevated risk of opioid overdose prevalent in the corrections population. This aligns with the current MOHLTC Provincial Opioid Strategy. The policy was released on April 17, 2018. Education was provided to health care staff via Adobe connects and a letter outlining the policy revisions was sent to physicians at the time of release.

Since this inquest, a new physician has been contracted at the Quinte DC for the MMT program. The Health Care Manager has provided the physician with the MCSCS MMT policy and procedure and reviewed the expectations. Further, the Health Care Manager has developed an action plan to ensure required processes are in place and followed. All Quinte DC nursing staff were provided the revised management of opioid withdrawal policy. Additional education sessions were done on May 2, 8 and 10, 2018 to ensure all nursing staff are trained and familiar with the policy revisions and expectations.

A nursing staff meeting took place on May 16, 2018 to ensure the nurses received the feedback from the physician regarding process, and review the plan with regard to the new MMT policy, and to ensure that nursing staff are aware of the changes and the immediate implementation. The Health Care Manager will audit 10 health care records weekly to ensure compliance with the management of opioid withdrawal policy. This process was initiated on May 14, 2018 and continues on a weekly basis.", "", "", "", "", "", ""]

["2018", "Q2018-01", "MCSCS", "3. More thorough assessment of incoming inmates during early incarceration period to ensure proper medical evaluation (i.e., COWS, urine panel test).", "The MCSCS has completed a review and revised the Management of Opioid Withdrawal policy and procedure. As part of the review, specific requirements for ongoing monitoring was added. The revised policy was released on April 17, 2018 and health care staff education was provided via webinar on April 17, 2018 and repeated on April 24, 2018. The ministry continues to engage and consult with community substance use experts to discuss strategies to safely and effectively manage opioid withdrawal.

The revised management of opioid withdrawal policy was also provided to the physician(s). The changes in requirements were reinforced during a nursing staff meeting on May 16, 2018. A urine drug panel testing is done before administering the first dose of methadone, and then random tests are done monthly. Where urinalysis is positive for drug or when an individual has symptoms of possible drug toxicity, the physician is consulted.

All new admissions are assessed by the primary care physician. When a physician is not on-site, the nurses will call the physician regarding an inmate's health condition, including concerns about substance use. The correctional staff notify the nurses of all new admissions and any medical concerns presented by the inmate. Based on the notification, the nurse conducts a first assessment, which consists of triaging the inmate's immediate health concerns and current medications followed by a more detailed evaluation, within 24 hours of admission. During medication rounds, the nurse assesses an inmate when a health care concern is identified. Additionally, the correctional officers notify the unit nurses if an inmate has a health concern, and the nurse assesses the inmate as soon as practicable.", "", "", "", "", "", ""]

["2018", "Q2018-01", "MCSCS", "4. We support the delivery of the MMT/medical services at Quinte Detention Centre, which should be provided in a timely manner.", "The Quinte DC supports the delivery of MMT/medical services in a timely manner. The primary care physician has on-site clinics three days a week, and the nurses triage and schedule the clients for these clinics. When the physician is not on-site, there is a physician on-call, and the nurses contact them regarding new admissions and if there are concerns regarding the health status of individuals. The MMT physician has an on-site clinic every two weeks, and the nurses call the physician regarding new admissions or other methadone related concerns. The Quinte DC submitted a business case on May 30, 2018 for additional methadone services to increase the MMT physician clinic to once a week to improve access to MMT services.", "", "", "", "", "", ""]

["2018", "Q2018-01", "Centre of Forensic Sciences (CFS)", "5. Centre of Forensic Sciences should have the ability to detect the presence/absence of all medication prescribed in a correctional facility.", "The Centre of Forensic Sciences (CFS) is able to detect and or quantitate a vast array of the most frequently encountered and forensically relevant over-the counter prescription, and recreational/illicit drugs. New drugs (both licit and illicit) are continually being developed and used for new purposes and it is not practical for the CFS to develop quantitation methods and purchase applicable standard reference samples for all drugs.

To prioritize the development of methods for new drugs that are significant in criminal and death investigations, CFS consults with agencies including Health Canada laboratories, Canadian Border Service Agency laboratories, the Office of the Chief Coroner of Ontario, Ontario Forensic Pathology Services and other forensic toxicology laboratories.

Although CFS has the ability to detect Paliperidone using a screening method, it does not have a method to confirm the concentration of the drug in post mortem samples. Although this drug was first introduced into the US in 2007, there have been few reports of any toxic effects reported with its use, and a consequent lack of data as to post-mortem blood concentrations associated with toxic and/or fatal concentrations. Thus, development of a method for quantitation of this drug at toxic and/or potentially fatal concentrations has not been possible or probative.

Reports issued by CFS Toxicology include the drug(s) detected, the methods used for the analysis and a link to a list of all of the drugs that were tested for. This allows the pathologist and/or coroner to have the sample tested by another laboratory if CFS does not have a method for a specific drug of interest.", "", "", "", "", "", ""]

["2018", "Q2018-02", "MCSCS", "1. Ensure correctional staff are trained regularly on the use of Naloxone including signs and symptoms of opioid overdose.", "Naloxone, both injectable and nasal, is currently available to Health Care staff in all correctional facilities. All institutions currently have nasal Naloxone kits available for use by trained sergeants in the event that health care staff are not available. The ministry is nearing completion of the training of correctional officers in the use of Intranasal Naloxone Spray as they will have access to the spray within correctional facilities ensuring its accessibility for the emergency treatment of suspected opioid overdose.", "", "", "", "", "", ""]

["2018", "Q2018-02", "MCSCS", "2. Ensure regular training of health care staff on withdrawal and toxicity of commonly abused drugs including the use of the CIWA and COWS scales.", "As of March 2017, the use of the Clinical Institute Withdrawal Assessment for Alcohol (CIWA-Ar) and the Clinical Opioid Withdrawal Scale (COWS) were included in the new nurses orientation and physician welcome packages (implemented in March 2017). The recommended clinical protocols for management of alcohol withdrawal and management of opioid withdrawal have been incorporated into the ministry's formulary. Corporate Health Care hosts regular training webinars to ensure that health care staff are familiar with the management of alcohol and opioid withdrawal policies and procedures, toxicity of commonly abused drugs, and the use of the CIWA-Ar and COWs scales. During the webinar, expectations for documentation were reinforced.", "", "", "", "", "", ""]

["2018", "Q2018-02", "MCSCS", "3. Use the facts of Mr. Sutton’s and Mr. Stevens’ deaths to develop case studies to train health care staff. This training should be designed, developed and delivered in collaboration with front line staff.", "Corporate Health Care, in collaboration with TSDC staff will develop case studies (including the facts of Mr. Sutton's and Mr. Stevens' deaths) and conduct webinars for health care staff with regard to the issues identified at this inquest.", "", "", "", "", "", ""]

["2018", "Q2018-02", "MCSCS", "4. Ensure regular training of health care staff on documentation standards set by the College of Nurses and Ministry expectations. This should include standards related to charting by exception.", "The College of Nurses of Ontario (CNO) is the governing body for all nurses employed in Ontario. The CNO publishes practice standards and guidelines for all nurses and nurses are expected to review and abide by these standards and guidelines in their practice setting. These practice standards include a standard on documentation and professional standards, as well as learning modules. Corporate Health Care does provide and arrange training on documentation, and the Health Care Manager, Toronto South Detention Centre (TSDC) has made arrangements for all nursing staff to review the CNO documentation standards. The Health Care Manager, TSDC, regularly reviews the health care services policies and procedures, which include documentation and communication procedures, with the health care team members.\n\nIt is part of the nursing professional obligations to pursue education outside the workplace. The MCSCS encourages employees to identify training needs and assistance required to meet these goals. TSDC nurses are encouraged to attend corporate health care in service training and case reviews. Regular educational sessions via the Ontario Telemedicine Network are also available to all nurses. They are presented by various disciplines and hospitals to promote current standards of practice.", "", "", "", "", "", ""]

["2018", "Q2018-02", "MCSCS", "6. Within twelve months from the date of this verdict, establish a working group of experts and senior Ministry staff to coordinate a strategic plan for reducing the risks from illicit drug use in custody, including and not limited to:
i) identifying harm reduction strategies that will be employed;
ii) tracking of fatal and non-fatal drug overdoses in custody; and
iii) the detection and screening methods to be employed such as x-rays and other new techniques to identify drugs concealed within the person.", "The MCSCS will continue to work with the Ministry of Health and Long-Term Care (MOHLTC) who are the lead for the provincial Opioid Strategy and other experts to develop strategies to reduce the risks from illicit drug use while clients are in custody. 

To date, MOHLTC and MCSCS have worked together to develop strategies to prevent opioid overdose:
- On January 30, 2017, an initial information session regarding the dangers of Opioid Overdose Risk and Prevention Strategies was conducted with every inmate in custody in an Ontario correctional institution. Health teaching is now conducted upon admission by nurses during the admission health assessment.
- All individuals admitted to an Ontario correctional institution have access to the Inmate Information Guide. Included in this guide is a section entitled "Tolerance to drugs and risk for overdose"""". This section provides inmates with information about the risks of Opioid and other drug use.""]

["As part of the MOHLTC province-wide strategy to address Opioid overdose", " the MCSCS has implemented a 'Take Home Naloxone' (THN) program in all facilities. The program", " which provides THN kits at discharge", " and includes health teaching on overdose risk", " signs of overdose and use of Naloxone", " is available to all inmates who are identified or identify as at-risk for opioid overdose and want to have a THN kit at discharge. Additionally", " visual aids (such as signage", " brochures and/or posters) and ad-hoc information sessions are used in institutions to enhance awareness of overdose risk. The MCSCS continues to work closely with MOHLTC on strategies to mitigate risk. The ministry tracks fatal and non-fatal drug overdoses on the inmate's medical file as well as any treatment provided."]

["In August 2015", " the ministry installed an x-ray body scanner at the TSDC. In May 2016 the ministry committed to installing x-ray scanners in every institution and as of August 2018", " all institutions except one have operational body scanners. The effective use of the technology can have a dramatic impact on the reduction of the amount of contraband that enters an institution.\"\"", "", "", "", "", "", ""]

["2018", "Q2018-02", "MCSCS", "8. Ensure correctional staff are trained on the requirement to communicate with other staff between shifts. This training should include the use of communication tools such as magnet indicators on segregation doors.", "Communication amongst all correctional staff, including health care is paramount. Staff are routinely reminded to review the Standing Orders to ensure they are aware of their obligations when they receive/have pertinent information on the well-being of an inmate. It is ministry policy that all employees responsible for the care of inmates alert the appropriate officials and take the appropriate steps if they believe that an inmate's well-being may be at risk (to themselves or to others). Observations are captured through the completion of required documentation (i.e., log book entries, occurrence reports, etc.) per ministry policy and procedures.

It is the responsibility of the officer being relieved from duty to share all pertinent information that occurred during the course of their shift. It is also the responsibility of the officer assuming duties to read the log book entries, observation sheets, etc. The facility has issued a memorandum to all staff to remind them of their responsibilities in this regard on April 4, 2017. A further memorandum was issued to managers regarding internal communications and log books on May 16, 2018.

Training on communication is imbedded into the COTA program. Recruits receive overarching material in their Self-Directed Learning package titled "Special Management Inmates"""". Specific training regarding the use of magnetic indicators on segregation doors is covered in the classroom instruction for the Special Management Inmates lesson."""", "", "", "", "", "", ""]

Areas, or segments of the coastline, where the first two variables (e.g., shoreline classification and REI) co-occurred were defined as ‘moderately suitable’ habitat, those where the first three variables (e.g., shoreline classification, REI, and bathymetry) co occurred were defined as ‘suitable’ habitat, and those where all four variables (e.g., shoreline classification, REI, bathymetry, and linear water flow features) co-occurred were defined as ‘highly suitable’ habitat.", "Trois classes qualitatives de favorabilité de l'habitat ont été définies en fonction du nombre de variables prédictives convergentes à chaque étape de l'analyse. Les zones ou segments de littoral où les deux premières variables (e.g., classification du littoral et IER) étaient présentes simultanément ont été définies comme un habitat « modérément favorable », celles où les trois premières variables (e.g., classification du littoral, IER et bathymétrie) étaient présentes simultanément ont été définies comme un habitat « favorable », et celles où les quatre variables (e.g., classification du littoral, IER, bathymétrie et courants d'eau linéaires) étaient présentes simultanément ont été définies comme un habitat « très favorable ».
